newsitem.title: POLAND: Kredyt eyes Lithuanian branch, not purchase.
newsitem.headline: Kredyt eyes Lithuanian branch, not purchase.

text.p: Polish Kredyt Bank SA has abandoned plans to buy a Lithuanian bank and applied to the Lithuanian central bank to open a branch there instead, Kredyt Bank's president said on Tuesday.
"There's a lower price and a lower risk when you open a branch than when you buy a bank," Stanislaw Pacuk told a news conference.
He said he hoped Kredyt Bank's prospective Lithuanian branch would handle roughly half of Polish-Lithuanian trade, which rose 35 percent last year to $260 million.
Kredyt Bank had previously said it might invest in ailing Lithuanian bank Litimpeks.

In June Lithuania passed legislation allowing foreign banks to open and a month later its central bank said Kredyt Bank had applied to open a branch and that the central bank had two months to give its decision.
On Tuesday Pacuk said Kredyt Bank still sought to buy up to 30 percent of a Russian bank either in Moscow or in the neighbouring Kaliningrad enclave by the end of the year.
Kredyt Bank currently has representative offices in Vilnius and Kaliningrad and holds a 13.3-percent stake in Kiev International Bank.
Belgian Kredietbank holds 7.2 percent of Kredyt.
